newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX crude called lower following IPE Brent.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX crude called lower following IPE Brent.

text.p: NYMEX crude was called lower early Monday following IPE Brent futures, while a weak cash market led to a lower call in heating oil, traders said.
Crude was called five to 10 cents lower a barrel while heating oil was called unchanged to 0.25 cent a gallon lower. Gasoline was called unchanged to 0.25 cent higher.

"Brent just collapsed late Friday, and crude is following through today," said a trader. AT 0918 EST, December Brent was 10 cents lower at $24.12 a barrel on the IPE. The higher call in nearby gasoline was attributed to technical strength.

"(November) Gasoline has held above 69.75 cents pretty well, so it's in good shape," said a trader. In contrast, November heat was seen running into resistance at around 72.00 cents, above which is a well-trodden trading channel.
"Heating oil will have a real test. We will have to see whether it can get back into the previous channel," said Refco Energy Group vice president Victor Yu.

Friday, December crude ended 35 cents higher at $24.86 a barrel while November heating oil settled 1.23 cents a gallon higher 71.72 cents. November gasoline closed up 0.88 cent a gallon to 70.10 cents.
Meanwhile, warmer weather in the northeast United States and a glut of distillate awaiting shipment from the U.S. Gulf has weakened spot heat prices in Houston.
"There is some weakness in the heat cash market that is taking it lower," said a trader of heating oil's call.
